what: The sections of this article, each with a line and a paragraph, for showing what the reader has already read. Built by admin/build/summaries.py from admin/content/articles/summaries/.

sections.label: The opening
sections.line: 53 site repositories, 45 live, 1,679 commits and 5,419 pages in eleven weeks.
sections.para: All the sgit.ai sites, counted on 21 October 2026: 53 repositories, 45 live, one built and not serving, seven placeholders. 1,679 commits, 33,541 files and 5,419 sitemap pages. Growth came in bursts of about ten new sites a week; four repositories hold 62% of the commits, and the median site has seven. Families of sites are appearing, so naming needs a rule.

sections.label: In short
sections.line: Six lines: 53 repositories, 45 live, 1,679 commits, 5,419 pages, bursts, a long tail.
sections.para: 53 repositories and 45 live sites, one built and not serving, seven placeholders. 1,679 commits since 11 August 2026. 5,419 pages in sitemaps and 33,541 files. About ten new sites in each of five weeks. Four repositories hold 62% of the commits; the median has seven. Hubs with instances are appearing, which is why naming needs a rule.

sections.label: The estate, counted
sections.line: The count: 45 live sites, one not serving, seven placeholders, and what they hold.
sections.para: All 53 repositories were read, all branches, and every host asked whether it answers. 45 are live on GitHub Pages; ux.sgit.ai is built and returns 404; seven are placeholders, two made this morning. 1,416 commits carry a version. 35 of 46 content repositories publish llms.txt, 41 live sites serve a sitemap, 33 publish a version.

sections.label: How it grew
sections.line: It grew in bursts of about ten sites a week, and the busiest commit week was 12 October.
sections.para: sgit.ai started on 11 August. Nine and ten new sites followed in late August, ten in the week of 7 September, a quieter September, then ten in the week of 12 October and eight in the week of 19 October. Commits peaked at 331 in the week of 12 October; the quietest week, of 28 September, had 60.

sections.label: Where the work is
sections.line: A long tail: four repositories hold 62% of the commits; the median site has seven.
sections.para: sgit.ai, the newsroom, graphs and PKI carry most of the work. 22 of the 46 content repositories have their whole history in one day: a site is built in a session and left to do its job. 22 were touched in the last week and 12 not since August. The ones used daily keep growing.

sections.label: Where the pages are
sections.line: Pages tell another story: the newsroom lists 1,282, its Portuguese edition 929.
sections.para: A site that renders a book or a corpus can be large and young at once. pt.newsroom.sgit.ai lists 929 pages from 74 commits, and the Gen Z Developers book site 496 pages from 70 commits in three days, while sgit.ai lists 604.

sections.label: Families, and the naming they need
sections.line: Families are appearing, and with them second-level hosts of three kinds.
sections.para: API sites hold a site's client code; editions are the same site for another language or audience; family instances sit under a hub. The instances were named inconsistently, so a rule was fixed on 21 October: plural for the hub, singular for the instance. Four hosts break it today, three providers and a game.

sections.label: What it says
sections.line: Sites are cheap, attention concentrates, hubs make families, and the loose ends are few.
sections.para: Most sites took a session or two, which is why there are 53. Four repositories carry most of the work. Several sites of one kind need a hub and a naming rule. The loose ends are visible: one site not serving, four without a sitemap, seven placeholders and four hosts to rename.

sections.label: What this does not claim
sections.line: Counts of one day; all branches; sitemaps list what sites choose; versions at the usual paths.
sections.para: The counts are of 21 October 2026 and change with every release. Commits include working branches later merged. Release commits are counted by a version in the subject. Sitemaps list what a site chooses to list, and a site may publish its version somewhere other than the usual paths.

sections.label: Where this comes from
sections.line: The git history and files of all 53 repositories, and every site's pages, read 21 October.
sections.para: The git history of the 53 SGit-AI__Website repositories, all branches, and the files at each head; each site's home page, sitemap, version file and DNS, checked on 21 October 2026; with related newsroom articles on naming, v0.12 and the release pipeline.
